title: Report terminal double-bar consumer loss without stripping authored XML
scope: Report the pinned AlphaTab loss of an authored final DoubleBar, retain the exact GPIF flag and Go round-trip value, and add terminal/nonterminal consumer regressions including the actual resolved line-style difference.
acceptance: Public Parse of testdata/gp4/Slides.gp4 retains final MeasureHeader.DoubleBar=true. Assert the final DoubleBar XML and Go reparse true. The pinned original binary consumer reports isDoubleBar=true, barLineRight=LightLight, and getActualBarLineRight()=LightLight; its exported GP8 consumer reports false, Automatic, and LightHeavy. Record these as distinct authored and consumer results, not equivalent projection.

For an otherwise report-free score with consistent header/measure compatibility flags and final DoubleBar=true, preflight emits one stable scoped consumer-omission report at the final master-bar location. Its reason identifies the authored flag retained in GPIF and the pinned consumer clearing it. Do not substitute the unrelated measure-double-bar-authority report.

Strict export returns no bytes while this consumer loss is unallowed. Allowing an unrelated code does not bypass it; allowing exactly the new terminal-double-bar consumer code succeeds and retains DoubleBar in XML and Go reparse, while independent consumption confirms the known limit.

A nonfinal DoubleBar remains true in exact XML, Go reparse, and pinned consumer and receives no terminal-loss report; final DoubleBar=false receives no terminal-loss report. A multi-bar true/false/true case proves correct report location and that only the final consumer flag changes. Keep existing authority-conflict behavior independently covered.

Extend the independent oracle with a dedicated raw DoubleBar/bar-line projection or direct scoped facts; the ordinary normalized oracle omits isDoubleBar. Register source, wire, consumer, and policy assertions in the semantic ledger. Update documentation and inventory to replace the prior unsupported equivalence statement; export remains partial.
exclusions: Do not erase authored DoubleBar XML to match AlphaTab. No global bar-line normalization, renderer implementation, screenshot requirement, or dependency on global stylesheet #109. No new custom-barline public API or invented retaining syntax.

reproduction.instructions: Public Parse and ExportWithReport testdata/gp4/Slides.gp4. Read original and exported bytes with pinned ScoreLoader and inspect masterBars[1].isDoubleBar plus tracks[0].staves[0].bars[1].barLineRight/getActualBarLineRight(). Original is true/LightLight/LightLight; target is false/Automatic/LightHeavy. Check the exact DoubleBar XML and Go true independently. For strict-policy isolation, use semanticValidPitchedGP8Song with Notation=true and consistent compatibility flags, set final DoubleBar=true, and inspect the currently empty report before adding the new scoped loss.

Record the consumer-only normalization and the verified tests/commit, then resolve this investigation when its checklist passes. If visual terminal-bar fidelity remains required, name a visual/retaining oracle as separate scope. This does not block #109 global stylesheet keys.

evidence.reference: TestNotationSlidesDoubleBar plus direct pinned Bar.getActualBarLineRight() probe
evidence.detail: On baseline8d72944, original Slides.gp4 final bar facts were isDoubleBar=true, requested LightLight, actual LightLight. Go-exported GP8 retained authored XML/Go flag but AlphaTab final facts were false, Automatic, LightHeavy. This disproves the old issue comment that terminal flag clearing is only an equivalent derived projection. Current fixture reports unrelated losses plus compatibility authority; clean authored three-bar probe emits no reports despite terminal flag loss.
